questions.q: Ten independent orders each have a 30% chance of being returned. Which distribution describes the number of returned orders?
questions.explain: You are counting successes (returns) in a fixed number of independent trials with a constant probability, which is the binomial setting.

questions.q: In scipy, what does stats.binom(10, 0.3).sf(4) compute?
questions.explain: sf is the survival function, 1 - cdf. With cdf(4) covering 4 or fewer, sf(4) is the chance of more than 4.

questions.q: A help desk gets an average of 4 tickets per hour. Which statement about a Poisson model of this is correct?
options: The mean is 4 but the variance is 16
The variance is 4, equal to the mean
The variance is 2, the square root of the mean
The variance depends on how many hours you observe
questions.explain: A Poisson distribution has mean and variance both equal to lambda. If real counts show a much larger variance, the model does not fit well.

questions.q: Each visitor converts with probability 0.2. What is the expected number of visitors until the first conversion?
questions.explain: For a geometric distribution the mean number of trials to the first success is 1/p = 1/0.2 = 5.

questions.q: Your simulated probability of exactly 3 returns is 0.2679 while the exact binomial value is 0.2668. What should you conclude?
options: The formula is wrong and must be fixed
The simulation is broken because it should match exactly
This is normal random noise; more simulated draws would usually get closer
The trials must not be independent
questions.explain: A simulation is a random sample, so it differs a little from the exact value. The gap tends to shrink as you draw more samples.
